Leave-one-out gate implemented and INDEPENDENTLY RECOMPUTED against real distributions (Strategy asked me not to trust their arithmetic). Not a rationalisation: the old rule (>=3 brands AND no brand >30%) was unsatisfiable at n=3, where the minimum possible largest share is 33.3%. It was a contradiction, not a threshold. BUT the new rule bounds no concentration at all — an angle could be 90% one brand and pass if the rest spans 3 brands / 5 ads. Defensible, but the pitch shows the drop arithmetic inline on every row rather than a bare pass mark.

CLAIM-POLICY CONTRACT QUESTION FOR STRATEGY — Agent 3 and Agent 5 read the brief differently and it is worth $117. My brief says rendered output carries no performance or medical claims ("we sell creative volume and angle coverage, never results"). Writer cleared 9 scripts whose claims_used include "studies show 22% younger skin", "93% experience better hair", "supports the skin barrier in 7 days" — Froya's own substantiated homepage copy, and a normal thing for an ad to say. I did NOT settle it: medical claims fail always with no switch; substantiated PERFORMANCE claims are governed by Config.allow_brand_substantiated_claims, defaulting to False because that fails closed. Improvised claims (in the render, not in the script) fail under either reading — that is the part only Agent 5 can catch.

FREE PRE-SCREEN CHANGES THE ESTIMATE MATERIALLY. Agent 5's content checks run against SCRIPT TEXT before any render, at $0. Under the strict default 5 of the 9 cleared scripts fail (customer_testimonial 01/02/03, heritage_origin-01, ingredient_villain-01). A content failure is in the copy, so it repeats on every re-render — those 5 consume the full 3-attempt cap and deliver nothing. Properly costed that is $160 at Creatify for FOUR usable videos, $117 of it burned; $195 at Seedance, $144 burned. Rewriting the copy first costs $0 and drops the batch to $43 (Creatify) / $51 (Seedance). The flat 20-40% reject rate is right for technical faults, which are random per render, and wrong for content failures, which are deterministic — so the estimator models them separately.

TWO REAL BUGS FOUND BY RUNNING IT, NOT BY READING IT; both would have spent money. (1) IDEMPOTENCY: the attempt number is part of the job_id, so a per-job terminal check minted a fresh id every run, missed the qa_pass record, and RE-RENDERED FINISHED WORK — ~$7.80 per completed script per re-run at Creatify, silently. Now keyed on the script, not the job. (2) FIXTURE CONTAMINATION: a $0 --fixture run's nine fake passes made the next real Creatify batch skip those nine scripts as "already done". Fixture output must never stand in for a real render. Fixed twice over — accepted renders are provider-scoped, and fixture state lives in its own directory. Regression test for each. Same fail-upward family as the three defaults bugs Writer logged.

Money rules as implemented. Dry-run is the default and execute() refuses a dry-run config outright. Ceiling checked three times: whole estimate vs ceiling pre-batch, again before EVERY individual call, and again after each call against what the provider actually charged. Exceeding aborts, never warns. Approval is a phrase containing the exact amount and batch fingerprint, typed at a TTY — not readable from argv or env, so a peer session (including Strategy) structurally cannot supply it; there is no --yes. The ledger commits the debit BEFORE the call, so a crash mid-call reads as spent, not free, and jobs left in flight block the next run until a human reconciles them against the provider dashboard. Corrupt ledger, unknown entry kind, unpriced provider, missing brand.md, absent client_ready: all BLOCK.

PER-BRAND CLAIM GATING IN, per Strategy's ruling. Global switch REMOVED — Config.allow_brand_substantiated_claims and --allow-brand-claims are both gone. Substantiation is now read per brand from that brand's brand.md '## Substantiated claims' section (qa/substantiation.py): one bullet per claim, "claim" — source. A bullet with NO source is dropped as an assertion, not honoured. A brand with no section gets strict behaviour — fails closed on absence of evidence, not on a default. Deliberate asymmetry with do-not-say: a missing do-not-say list BLOCKS (we cannot tell what is forbidden); a missing substantiation list does not (no permissions on file is a complete, safe answer). 92 tests pass, still zero spend.

Rule as implemented. ALWAYS FAIL, no switch: medical claims (outranks substantiation — Froya publishes "Heals skin barrier in 7 days" on one SKU, a drug claim whoever published it); improvised claims (in the render, not in the approved script); STRENGTHENING — rounding up, extrapolating, combining two published claims, or attaching an unstated timeframe. "93%" cannot become "almost everyone"; "results in 60 days" cannot become "results in weeks". Strengthening fires whether or not the base claim is substantiated, because the strengthened version is a different claim the brand never made.

APPLIED TO TODAY'S DATA THE BATCH IS STILL GATED, ON EVIDENCE NOT ON A SWITCH. No brand.md in the repo carries a '## Substantiated claims' section, so all 25 brands are strict and 5 of 9 Froya scripts still fail — every failure now reads "unsubstantiated: brand.md does not record this claim with a source". NOT a policy problem and not Producer's to fix: 16 of the 17 claims the scripts use are ALREADY in Agent 0's raw capture (data/raw/intake/froyaorganics_com.json) VERBATIM, they were simply never rendered into brand.md. ONE BOUNDARY CALL FOR STRATEGY, flagged not buried. 'combined' currently fires when two published claims share a SENTENCE — e.g. "Studies show 22% younger skin, and 95% reported youthful glow", where each claim is individually substantiated. That is the conservative reading of "combining two claims into a stronger one"; a narrower reading would block only true fusion (a timeframe from one grafted onto the outcome of another), which is what the rule most clearly targets. Applied literally because the fix is one punctuation mark and a false negative is a regulatory claim. It accounts for all 3 remaining failures once substantiation exists. Narrowing it is Strategy's call, not mine.

CAUGHT MYSELF OVER-MATCHING — the mirror of the fail-closed bug family. My first 'universal' amplifier pattern matched a bare "anyone" and flagged Froya's own line "Buy two if anyone else lives with you", which would have pulled a clean script out of the batch. My README had asserted over-matching is cheap; that holds for a do-not-say term a human reviews and is FALSE in the pre-screen, which EXCLUDES scripts from the batch — an over-broad rule there costs a deliverable, not one glance. Amplifiers now must attach to a result. Also corrected my own inference: I assumed Agent 3 had softened "heals" to "supports"; it had not, both are Froya's own copy on different SKUs. Checked before writing it down.
